**Albert Einstein** (1879–1955) was a `German-born theoretical physicist` who revolutionized modern science by developing the **theory of relativity** and making foundational contributions to **quantum mechanics** . He won the **1921 Nobel Prize in Physics** for explaining the photoelectric effect.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein)[[2]](https://www.alberteinstein.com/)

### Major Scientific Contributions

- **Special Relativity (1905).** Einstein showed that space and time are linked into a single continuum and change depending on an object's speed.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Zn9M8bjB4s)
- **Mass-Energy Equivalence (E = mc²).** Derived from special relativity, this famous equation proves that small amounts of mass can convert into massive amounts of energy.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Zn9M8bjB4s)
- **Photoelectric Effect (1905).** He demonstrated that light travels in discrete energy packets called photons, laying the groundwork for quantum theory.[[1]](https://www.facebook.com/nobelprize/videos/did-you-know-we-can-thank-physics-laureate-albert-einstein-in-part-for-our-smart/805492161962539/)
- **Brownian Motion (1905).** His mathematical explanation of particles suspended in fluid provided decisive proof that atoms exist.[[1]](https://www.ias.edu/albert-einstein-brief)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_DLYu53GyAA&t=33)
- **General Relativity (1915).** Einstein redefined gravity not as an invisible force, but as the curving of spacetime caused by massive objects like stars and planets.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Zn9M8bjB4s)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvQrDToUPoU)

### Early Life & Career

- **Birth & Education.** Born on March 14, 1879, in Ulm, Germany, Einstein studied physics and mathematics at the [Swiss Federal Polytechnic School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ETH_Zurich) in Zurich.
- **The "Miracle Year."** While working as a patent clerk in Bern in 1905, he published four groundbreaking papers that transformed modern physics.
- **Academic Rise.** Following his 1905 breakthroughs, he held prestigious professorships in Zurich, Prague, and Berlin before leading the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_DLYu53GyAA&t=33)[[3]](https://www.ias.edu/albert-einstein-brief)

### Later Years & Legacy

- **Move to the United States.** Fleeing the rise of the Nazi regime in 1933, Einstein emigrated to the U.S. and joined the [Institute for Advanced Study](https://www.ias.edu/albert-einstein-brief) in Princeton, New Jersey. He became a U.S. citizen in 1940.
- **World War II & Pacifism.** Despite his lifelong pacifism, he signed a 1939 letter to President Franklin D. Roosevelt warning that Germany might build nuclear weapons, which helped spark the Manhattan Project. He was excluded from working on the project himself due to security concerns and later campaigned fiercely for nuclear disarmament.
- **Personal Life & Death.** He married Mileva Marić in 1903, with whom he had three children, before divorcing and marrying his cousin Elsa Löwenthal in 1919. Einstein died on April 18, 1955, at age 76 in Princeton.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein)[[2]](https://www.ias.edu/albert-einstein-brief)[[3]](https://www.osti.gov/opennet/manhattan-project-history/People/Scientists/albert-einstein.html)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvQrDToUPoU)
